info.bio:
Grupo de culto estadounidense formado en Cincinnati en 1986 y liderado por el vocalista, guitarra rítmica y compositor Greg Dulli. 
Compuesto a su vez por Rick McCollum (guitarra solista), John Curley (bajo) y Steve Earle (batería). 

Disueltos en 2001 gozaron de una popularidad limitada en los 90 que ha ido creciendo a lo largo de los años por los posteriores proyectos de Dulli y sobre todo por álbumes como Gentlemen (1993) o Black Love (1996)

scenes.name: Roots-rock de los ochenta y cow-punk
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Como en 1970 tras 1966, la new wave de 1976 va seguida de un revival del roots-rock, esta vez gradual y disfrazado: punks que desfiguran los estilos tradicionales (X, Dream Syndicate, Gun Club) y los «cow-punks» que tocan country ambientado entre inadaptados: Long Ryders, Jason & The Scorchers, Fetchin Bones, Lone Justice, Beat Farmers. El populismo de Los Lobos, Del Fuegos, Del-Lords y Walkabouts; en la Costa Oeste, los dementes Camper Van Beethoven, Donner Party, Catheads, Thin White Rope y los American Music Club de Mark Eitzel; en Texas, Wild Seeds, Poi Dog Pondering, Glass Eye; en los Grandes Lagos, BoDeans, Soul Asylum, Afghan Whigs, Shrimp Boat y los canadienses Cowboy Junkies. Nashville se renueva con los neotradicionalistas (George Strait, Randy Travis, Garth Brooks, Lyle Lovett, Steve Earle, Dwight Yoakam) y el surf instrumental vuelve con Shadowy Men On A Shadowy Planet.

podcast.title: "Four Minutes and 33 Seconds" Cover
podcast.body: The Afghan Whigs were among the artists who contributed to a 2019 box set by Mute Records, compiling various covers of John Cage's silent composition, "Four Minutes and 33 Seconds." "mute records compiled a bunch of them in a box set featuring... afghan wigs..."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 60 Mind Blowing Facts in 60 Minutes: The 5th Edition

podcast.title: Collaboration with Bob Rock
podcast.body: The Afghan Whigs are listed among Bob Rock's clients. "We got the cult, Veruch assault, Erasmith, Motley crew, Ardady Pease, the Tea Party, Eric and High Fy, Afghan Wigs, David Lee Roth, the Conorline Crush, Cher."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Musical Influence on Matthew Good
podcast.body: Afghan Whigs were a significant influence on Matthew Good's songwriting, particularly in their approach to the bass guitar. He noted their use of the bass as a "straight A instrument" that moved in steps, which contrasted with the more melodic bass lines of 60s and 70s music he also admired. "But also someone that was massively influenced by bands like The Pixies and the Replacements and Afghan Wigs and that kind of things. It was a straight A instrument."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Matt Good: In His Own Words - Part 2

xref.title: Covers Compilation Box Set (2019)
xref.body: In 2019, Mute Records released a box set featuring various artists covering John Cage's "Four Minutes and 33 Seconds." The compilation included more than 50 artists, such as Depeche Mode, New Order, Moby, Erasure, and Afghan Whigs, all performing a piece consisting of silence. "More than 50 artists playing nothing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: 60 Mind Blowing Facts in 60 Minutes: The 5th Edition
